title_en: The Relation of the Science of Logic to the Affirmation of God's Oneness
body_ar:
ما علاقة علم المنطق بالتوحيد؟

أن علم المنطق هو علم المقاييس العقلية التي يدرك بها الإنسان الأدلة العقلية، فمرجع المنطق إلى التفريق بين التصور والتصديق، والتصور هو إدراك المفردات والتصديق هو إدراك النسب، والتصور إنما يوصل إليه بالمعرفات والتصديق إنما يوصل إليه بالحجج، وهذه الأمور إذا عرفها الإنسان عرف ما هو دليل عقلا وما يحتاج إلى الإثبات وما لا يحتاج إليه وعرف الخطأ في الأدلة وطريقة تركيب الأدلة، فهو معيار ليس فيه محذور شرعا في التوحيد ولا في غيره، لكن يمكن أن يستغل في الخير ويمكن أن يستغل في الشر، فتعلمه مثل تعلم الرياضيات مثل تعلم الحساب مثل تعلم الكتابة هو من المعايير التي يمكن أن يكال بها السمن ويكال بها الخمر ويكال بها اللبن، فبحسب استغلاله.
body_en:
What is the relation of the science of logic to the affirmation of God's oneness (tawḥīd)?

The science of logic is the science of the rational measures by which a person grasps rational proofs. Logic comes back to the distinction between conception (taṣawwur) and assent (taṣdīq). Conception is the grasp of single terms; assent is the grasp of the relations between them. Conception is arrived at only by way of definitions (muʿarrifāt), and assent only by way of proofs (ḥujaj). When a person knows these matters, he knows what counts as a proof rationally, what stands in need of demonstration and what does not; and he knows where error enters into proofs, and how proofs are put together. So it is an instrument of measurement in which there is nothing objectionable in the revealed law, neither in tawḥīd nor in anything else — but it can be turned to good use and it can be turned to evil use. Learning it is like learning mathematics, like learning arithmetic, like learning writing: it is one of those measures with which clarified butter may be measured out, and wine may be measured out, and milk may be measured out. It goes according to the use that is made of it.

flags.arabic: فهو معيار ليس فيه محذور شرعا
flags.context: the Sheikh's own verdict on studying logic
options: render literally as 'there is nothing objectionable in it in the revealed law'
flags.note: The Sheikh deliberately does not use any of the five ruling terms here. He says there is no maḥdhūr (nothing to be guarded against) in it in the revealed law, and then makes the verdict depend entirely on use. Rendering this as 'permissible (mubāḥ)' would assign a five-rulings category he did not assign, and would lose the conditionality of his answer.

flags.arabic: معيار / المعايير ... يكال بها السمن ويكال بها الخمر ويكال بها اللبن
flags.context: the closing image comparing logic to a measuring vessel
options: instrument of measurement / measures (with which ghee, wine and milk may be measured out)
flags.note: miʿyār here is the concrete measuring vessel, not an abstract criterion: the point of the image is that the same vessel measures out a lawful substance and an unlawful one. 'Criterion' or 'yardstick' loses the concrete figure and with it the argument.

The question is stated in the body itself; the title restates it. Nothing has been supplied.
taṣawwur and taṣdīq are the standard pair in Arabic logic. They have been rendered 'conception' and 'assent' and the Arabic kept in brackets, since no settled English pair exists.
The Sheikh gives no ruling on the five-rulings scale and none has been supplied. See the flag.
